classification_definitions.ACTIVE_RUNTIME: Demonstrably consumed by a mounted endpoint and/or the frontend-served CineGlobe production path.
classification_definitions.IMPLEMENTED_NOT_ACTIVE: Executable implementation exists but the served CineGlobe path does not consume it.
classification_definitions.PARTIAL: Useful behavior exists, but the stated capability or its end-to-end handoff is incomplete.
classification_definitions.LEGACY: Mounted or retained implementation superseded by, or disconnected from, the canonical served path.
classification_definitions.TEST_ONLY: Only exercised as a fixture, test, or demo and not by served runtime.
classification_definitions.SCHEMA_ONLY: Persistence or transport shape exists without an active producer/consumer path.
classification_definitions.UNKNOWN: Repository evidence is insufficient to classify.

executive_conclusion.script: CineGlobe can deterministically parse raw screenplay text into coarse headings, heading-derived locations, character cues, counts and chunks, but that parser is not called by upload, project, or served optimizer paths. The active ProductionPackage layer only reshapes supplied facts and keeps missing facts unknown. No production-breakdown engine exists beyond coarse parser fields and hand-curated Little Utopia facts.
executive_conclusion.schedule: No schedule parser, schedule model, stripboard, shoot-day estimator, grouping engine, or schedule-to-cost handoff exists. Schedule is only a classified document/material-presence category plus unrelated eligibility and constraint fields.
executive_conclusion.budget_cost: CSV budget import and strong deterministic Movie Magic/EP PDF-text parsing exist. The canonical served Little Utopia runtime uses a verified 44-account snapshot rather than the generic import pipeline. Jurisdiction cost normalization is active, but is based on unsourced static 2024-2025 indices and generic default crew/budget assumptions, not actual rate cards.
executive_conclusion.bridge: The manual Bridge workflow, provider provenance, validation, persistence, reconciliation and human disposition are reusable. Script analysis and prebudget operation names are reserved but explicitly unsupported; script-specific packages, response schemas and element reconciliation must be extended.

unresolved_architecture_questions: Which input formats are mandatory for the first active screenplay path: FDX, screenplay PDF, Fountain, Final Draft text, or a bounded subset?
Should ScreenplayDocument remain the typed canonical script root, or should typed extraction attach directly to universal DocumentVersion with ScreenplayDocument as a projection?
What stable identifier/versioning policy governs scenes and extracted elements across revised drafts?
Which extracted elements require explicit user confirmation before they can affect schedule/cost?
What schedule interchange formats and user-authored schedule source will be canonical?
Will Level 1-3 estimates share BudgetLineItem or use a distinct estimate-line model so actual and estimated lines cannot be confused?
What verified external datasets and licensing terms will replace the static local-cost assumptions?
How should city/region/union/season/vendor-specific rates resolve beneath country-level cost profiles?
Where should the universal source-precedence resolver live so ingestion, estimates and optimizer consume the same controlling values?
How should a generalized multi-project state builder replace the current Little Utopia-only in-memory state without reopening the optimizer itself?
What screenplay confidentiality, retention and redaction requirements govern Bridge package export?
